title: ModSecurity v3 validator can accept mutable tracked source bytes hidden by Git index flags
title_de: ModSecurity-v3-Validator kann durch Git-Index-Flags versteckte veränderliche getrackte Source-Bytes akzeptieren
protocol: Git checkout provenance and immutable build-input materialization
profile: Parent PR #55 runtime-evidence remediation, isolated Framework candidate based on 784977615acfc55567e37b863309abc4a38ac877
technical_claim: Before remediation, ci_modsecurity_v3_require_clean_checkout accepted an empty git status result as proof that an existing checkout's working tree matched the pinned Git objects. A tracked file marked assume-unchanged can be changed without appearing in ordinary status. The direct, Apache, and NGINX consumers then copy and execute the mutable working tree. A post-validation source replacement has the same sink because the validated pathname, rather than an immutable source-object snapshot, was copied.
entry_point: Apache, NGINX, and direct ModSecurity v3 build paths accept an existing MODSECURITY_V3_SOURCE_DIR, validate it, then create a build copy that executes build.sh, configure, and make.
source_to_sink_or_broken_control: A caller-controlled existing checkout sets git update-index --assume-unchanged on a tracked build input and changes its working-tree bytes. ci_modsecurity_v3_require_clean_checkout calls git status --porcelain and receives no output, while root/child HEAD and Gitlink checks inspect index identity. build-v3-under-src.sh, prepare-apache-build.sh, and prepare-nginx-build.sh then copy the mutable MODSECURITY_V3_SOURCE_DIR and execute its build scripts.
attacker_prerequisites: Ability to cause a Framework consumer to accept a pre-existing MODSECURITY_V3_SOURCE_DIR.
Write access to a tracked file and the local Git index of that checkout before validation, or the ability to replace the supplied source path after validation.
observed_behavior: A task-owned real-Git fixture committed build.sh containing approved-source, marked it assume-unchanged, and changed its working tree to unapproved-source. Ordinary status was empty and ci_modsecurity_v3_require_clean_checkout returned 0. git ls-files -v reported lower-case h for build.sh, while HEAD and the working tree contained different bytes.
expected_behavior: A Framework consumer must never copy or execute mutable working-tree bytes merely because a checkout claims the reviewed HEAD. Unsafe assume-unchanged or skip-worktree index state must fail closed, and build input must be materialized from the approved root and approved recursive child Git objects into the task-owned destination rather than copied from the supplied working tree.
impact: An actor controlling an existing source checkout can cause arbitrary build input such as build.sh, configure, or a Makefile to be copied and executed with the Framework build or CI identity despite the pinned root and child commits. This is a high-impact supply-chain provenance bypass. No Parent, authoritative Framework, or MRTS checkout was used for the proof.
preconditions: A Framework build path accepts an existing MODSECURITY_V3_SOURCE_DIR.
The supplied checkout passes the pinned origin, detached HEAD, and recursive topology checks.
A tracked source file is modified after Git marks it assume-unchanged, or the source path changes after validation.
reproduction: Create a task-owned disposable Git repository with a committed build.sh containing approved-source.
Run git update-index --assume-unchanged build.sh and change build.sh to unapproved-source.
Observe an empty git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all --ignore-submodules=none result and lower-case h from git ls-files -v build.sh.
Source the isolated candidate ci/lib/common.sh and call ci_modsecurity_v3_require_clean_checkout; before remediation it returns 0 although HEAD and the working-tree build.sh differ.

evidence.command: RTK-wrapped task-owned Git assume-unchanged fixture followed by ci_modsecurity_v3_require_clean_checkout
evidence.summary: The pre-fix guard returned 0 while ordinary status was empty, ls-files -v reported h build.sh, HEAD contained approved-source, and the working tree contained unapproved-source.

evidence.command: RTK-wrapped focused provenance suite, Framework Make provenance contract, CI-root bootstrap suite, public-parent placeholder control, documentation checks, and full Framework lint
evidence.summary: Post-fix local controls passed: 24 focused provenance tests, immutable approved-object snapshots without .git metadata, direct/Apache/NGINX object-materialization wiring, full lint, and independent review without a remaining high or critical cross-UID blocker.

root_cause: The validator trusted normal Git status and index/Gitlink identity as a proxy for all consumed working-tree bytes. Git's assume-unchanged and skip-worktree flags weaken that proxy. The consumers separately copied the validated pathname, leaving a validation-to-copy replacement interval.
proposed_remediation: The local candidate now rejects any non-normal Git index flag before treating a checkout as clean and materializes each accepted root and static approved child from its pinned Git commit object through the hardened Git wrapper and tar into a private task-owned build destination, excluding Git metadata. Every direct ModSecurity v3 cp -a source copy is replaced by this object-based materialization, with real-Git hidden-byte, immutable-snapshot, public-parent, and legitimate-topology regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A lower-case assume-unchanged or skip-worktree index state causes ci_modsecurity_v3_require_clean_checkout to return 77 before a build action.
The direct, Apache, and NGINX consumers do not use cp -a on MODSECURITY_V3_SOURCE_DIR for executable build input.
Each materialized root and static approved child is generated from its exact pinned Git object through ci_modsecurity_v3_git and contains no .git metadata.
A real Git fixture with changed working-tree bytes materializes the approved committed bytes, not the changed bytes.
The clean exact approved eight-child topology remains a legitimate control and focused security, syntax, documentation, Change Record, Make, lint, and independent bypass review checks pass.
validation_plan: Run the new real-Git assume-unchanged regression before and after the index-flag rejection control.
Run the new real-Git object-materialization regression with changed working-tree bytes and confirm the output contains only the committed bytes and no .git metadata.
Run the full hermetic ModSecurity v3 provenance suite, shell syntax, the Framework provenance contract Make target, documentation, Change Record, and lint checks.
Perform an independent change-aware security review covering index flags, object materialization, source replacement, root/child archive coverage, tar extraction, and the existing local-Git controls.
legitimate_control_tests: A real Git object snapshot contains the committed approved-source build.sh even when the supplied working tree contains unapproved-source.
The clean exact approved root plus eight initialized pinned children materializes and builds through the direct Framework consumer without submodule mutation.
bypass_review: Review assume-unchanged and skip-worktree index states, staged/unstaged/untracked changes, source replacement after validation, root and nested child object archives, tar output confinement, recursive topology coverage, Git metadata exclusion, local configuration, remotes, detached HEADs, gitdir containment, path traversal, and symlink controls.
dependencies: Task-owned retained source evidence and Framework-local validation environment
deduplication_note: Not a duplicate of FND-FRAMEWORK-0032: that finding owns repository-controlled Git configuration execution and Git metadata mutation during inspection. This finding owns a distinct source-byte integrity and validation-to-copy boundary: hidden mutable working-tree bytes can reach build execution despite a pinned Git identity.
evidence_limitations: The dynamic proof changes only a task-owned benign fixture and never executes the changed file.

The related source-replacement race is source-to-sink validated but has not yet been dynamically raced; the object-snapshot control is selected because it eliminates reliance on post-validation working-tree bytes.
residual_risk: The cross-UID hidden-index and validation-to-copy boundary is fixed locally. Portable path-based shell controls cannot isolate a concurrent same-UID writer, so that limitation remains documented. A separate Framework PR, exact-head checks/review/Sonar evidence, Framework-master verification, and a separately authorized Parent gitlink update remain required before this finding can become verified or unblock Parent PR #55 runtime evidence. No Framework master, Parent gitlink, or MRTS action has occurred.

history.detail: A disposable fixture showed an empty status and lower-case h index flag while ci_modsecurity_v3_require_clean_checkout returned 0 for changed build.sh bytes. Source-to-sink review established later direct/Apache/NGINX copy-and-execute consumers.

The issue is distinct from FND-FRAMEWORK-0030 topology availability and FND-FRAMEWORK-0032 local Git configuration execution. It is P0/high/validated, in_progress, and blocks Framework delivery and Parent PR #55 runtime evidence until fixed and verified.

The candidate rejects assume-unchanged and skip-worktree flags, materializes all executable v3 input from pinned Git objects, passed 24 focused provenance tests, the Make contract, full Framework lint, documentation checks, retained object-snapshot control, and an independent review with no remaining high or critical cross-UID blocker. Status is fixed, not verified, because no Framework PR or master verification exists.
